name: A History of Glockmund
summary: The town's past. The player pieces it together from the market notice board, tavern rumors, chapel confessions, and a noble's library.

events.when: about eleven years ago, at the Harvest Feast
events.title: The Last Burning
events.content: Eleven years ago, at the Harvest Feast, the town burned a 'witch' — a lone herb-and-spice woman, accused of making a neighbor's cow miscarry and the well water turn bitter. A young priest led the trial. The old folk only lower their voices now: 'She smiled the whole way to the stake, and said she had done nothing at all.'
events.hook: The name of that young priest who led the trial matches the inquisitor, Severin. The hand on the new wanted notice looks like the same hand too.

events.title: Rise and Fall of the Spice Guild
events.content: Glockmund once grew rich on spice, set where two trade roads crossed; the guild could sway the town council. Then the eastern road shifted, the guild declined, and only House Walzer still buys rare goods, keeping its fixation on 'the scent of far places.' Half of Ode the taxman's harshness is that the town coffers truly are empty.
events.hook: The Count's high prices and his fixation on old instruments are rooted in this decline — he is buying back a vanished prosperity.
discover_via: an old vendor in the market

events.title: The Bitter Year
events.content: Seven years ago a fever swept Glockmund and killed near a third of its people. The church grew on it, calling the plague a judgment on the town for 'harboring something unclean.' Ever since, outsiders, the masked, and those who do not sleep at night are watched the closest.
events.hook: This is why Garen remembers every face, and why a masked cloak is conspicuous — this town has been trained by fear.
discover_via: the names of the dead carved at the chapel
